newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI shifts to buying dlrs in forward markets.
newsitem.headline: India RBI shifts to buying dlrs in forward markets.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Tuesday bought forward dollars after several months of spot-dollar purchases, bankers said.
"They started off by buying in the spot market as usual today," said the chief forex dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay. "But they then suddently shifted to buying outright May."
The chief dealer at a state-run bank said the RBI could have changed its stance in view of the consequences of its spot dollar buying on the money market.
"In one stroke, they are supporting the dollar without releasing rupees," he said. RBI would have to pay rupees for its forward purchases only in May, he said.
RBI's dollar purchases from the spot market was adding to the money supply at a time when banks are flush with funds.
Overnight call money has been trading at less than 5.0 percent in recent weeks. Call rates closed at 2.50-2.75 percent on Tuesday.
A dealer said the RBI was unnecessarily paying premium for its forward deals as the rupee may not depreciate even in May.
The RBI action was a catalyst in pushing up premia in the forward market on Tuesday.
The six month annualised forward premium closed Tuesday at 6.47 percent, up from the previous 6.25 percent.
The spot dollar closed almost steady at 35.850/855 rupees.
The RBI bought spot dollars in the morning but its buying had little effect against a backdrop of abundant dollar supplies and lack of import covering, dealers said.
